detailed_rationale:
Tega Industries makes polymer-based mill liners and other consumables for mineral beneficiation, mining and bulk-solids handling - the world's second-largest producer of polymer mill liners by revenue, with consumables making up ~86% of revenue (a recurring, 'critical-to-operate' replacement-part model that is structurally a decent moat). That said, the recent operating trend is going the wrong way: Q4 FY26 (Mar 2026) sales were Rs 527cr with OPM of only 11%, and full FY26 sales of Rs 1,692cr carried a 14% OPM and Rs 143cr PAT - both margin levels well below what a scaled consumables business of this quality should be printing. Screener's own flags are blunt: 3-year profit CAGR is -8% and 5-year compounded profit growth is effectively 0%, despite revenue continuing to grow (1yr revenue growth per the quant sheet is a modest 3.3%, decelerating sharply from the 11.7% 3-year CAGR).

The quant sheet's ROE/ROCE figures (14.2%/17.3%) read more favorably than screener's current-year figures (ROE 5.94%, ROCE 8.09%) - this is a case of the scorecard capturing an older, better period before the recent margin compression; the live figures are the ones to trust for judgment purposes. Balance sheet metrics remain conservative (D/E ~0.12, interest coverage ~10x), so this is a margin/execution problem, not a leverage problem. A minor one-off: Tega's Chilean subsidiary lost a tax-loss appeal at a local tribunal, with an estimated exposure of ~Rs 8.73cr - immaterial against ~Rs 1,700cr of sales, not a thesis-changing item.

The more persistent concern is promoter stake, which has fallen from 79.17% (Mar 2022) to 67.51% (Jun 2026) - a meaningful ~11.6 point reduction over four years that is worth tracking even though it has not been tied here to any specific negative disclosure. At ~82.7x trailing earnings, the stock is priced for a much better margin trajectory than the company has actually delivered over the last three years.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold on both windows, and the fundamentals argue for staying there rather than moving in either direction: the consumables-led business model and moat are real, but a negative 3-year profit CAGR against a rich ~83x earnings multiple rules out anything constructive, while the recurring-revenue mix, conservative balance sheet and lack of any solvency-level red flag rule out a Sell-grade concern. This is squarely a 'prove the margin recovery' Hold, which the quant score already reflects via a weak growth_1y_score (19.1) against a merely middling quality_score (45.6).
summary: Tega Industries makes mill liners and other wear parts for the mining industry - a recurring, replacement-driven consumables business with a real competitive position (second-largest globally). However, profit growth has actually gone backwards over the last three years even as revenue ticked up, and margins in the latest quarter (11% operating margin) are well below the company's historical levels. At roughly 83x trailing earnings, we don't think the current valuation is justified until the margin trend actually turns, so we rate it a Hold.
positive_para: The consumables model (86% of revenue) is a genuine strength - mill liners wear out and must be replaced to keep mining operations running, which gives Tega recurring, less-discretionary revenue and global scale as the number-two polymer liner maker. Balance sheet health is solid (low debt, ~10x interest coverage), giving management room to invest through the mining capex cycle without financial stress, and the underlying end-market (global mining capex/production) has structural tailwinds from continued metals and minerals demand.
negative_para: The number that should worry a holder most is the 3-year profit CAGR of -8% - this is not a company whose earnings have been compounding, despite steady revenue growth, and the latest quarter's 11% operating margin confirms the pressure is current, not historical. Paying ~83x trailing earnings for a business with that profit trajectory requires a real margin-recovery call that hasn't shown up in the numbers yet, and the promoter stake reduction from ~79% to ~67.5% over four years, while not proof of anything specific, is a trend worth watching rather than dismissing.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~83x trailing earnings against a -8% three-year profit CAGR, the multiple is pricing a margin recovery back toward Tega's historically higher operating margins that has not yet materialized in the reported numbers - this reads as rich relative to what the business has actually delivered lately, fair only if one is confident the recent margin compression is cyclical (mining capex softness) rather than structural (competitive/pricing pressure).
